title: Determinantal evaluation of the N-variable complex Gamma sum-integral with pole-separated contours and the explicit unbarred/barred convergence bounds
author: Sergey E. Derkachov; Alexander N. Manashov
source_version: Official SIGMA 16 (2020) article 003, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2020.003; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: The direct proof transforms a multidimensional discrete-continuous integral into a determinant of Mellin moments. It factors a coupled residue/discrete sum into two multivariate hypergeometric sums, then resolves the permutation signs and a sine-sum cancellation to obtain the Gamma product. Control of contour poles, absolute convergence and the two independent residue sectors is essential beyond applying an ordinary one-dimensional Barnes identity.

retained_original_metadata.statement_scope: Identity(2.3a) for N>=1, integer discrete parts of all u,z,w as fixed in Section2.1, Gamma(u,bar_u)=Gamma(u)/Gamma(1-bar_u) with bar_u a paired parameter, not assumed complex conjugation. Use contours separating the two specified pole strings and the stricter explicit proof conditions sum Re(z_k+w_k)<1 AND sum Re(bar_z_k+bar_w_k)<1 from(2.12), in the absolutely convergent pole-separated regime of(2.8). The conclusion is exactly the displayed Gamma-product evaluation, including 1/N! and sum/integration measure.
